findings.location: src/haute/deploy/_scorer.py:605-704 (MODEL_SCORE branch of _intercept) + fall-through to haute._builders._build_model_score
findings.title: Misconfigured modelScore node deploys and serves as a SILENT passthrough — the 'no model artifact' fail-loud guard is bypassed when neither model nor contract is bundled
findings.description: The deploy scorer's stated invariant (lines 673-702) is that 'deployed scoring cannot produce predictions without a model artifact' and 'Deploy scoring must never manufacture null predictions when no real model artifact is available.' This guard (model_score_missing_artifact, raising RuntimeError) ONLY fires when a feature contract was bundled (`if bundled_contract_path is not None`, line 677). If a modelScore node is misconfigured so that the bundler skips it entirely (no model AND no contract bundled), the intercept's MODEL_SCORE branch finds remapped_path=None and bundled_contract_path=None, returns None (line 733), and falls through to the base `_build_node_fn` -> `_build_model_score`, which returns `_passthrough_fn` for unconfigured sources (_builders.py:1170-1175). The deployed node then passes its input through UNCHANGED, producing an API response that silently omits the model's prediction column, with NO error raised at build, serve, or contract-enforcement time.
findings.evidence: Trace: (1) Bundler `collect_artifacts` (_bundler.py:70-103) defaults sourceType to 'run'; for sourceType=='run' with empty run_id or artifact_path it does `continue` (lines 90-91), and for sourceType=='registered' with empty registered_model it logs a warning and `continue`s (lines 79-83) — in both cases NO `{nid}__<model>` artifact and NO `{nid}__feature_contract.json` are added to the artifact map. (2) At serve time HauteModel.predict (_model_code.py:49-57) calls score_graph with exactly the bundled artifact_paths and the manifest's output_fields (which may be None). (3) In _scorer.py _intercept, for that node remap has no `{nid}__...` keys, so `bundled_contract_path` (line 606) and `remapped_path` (line 607) are both None; neither the model_score_fn branch (line 629) nor the model_score_missing_artifact branch (line 677) is entered; the function returns None at line 733. (4) wrap_builder then calls the base `_build_node_fn`; `_build_model_score` (_builders.py:1163-1175) returns `_passthrough_fn` because `source_type=='run' and not _run_id`. (5) In _execute_lazy the node runs `fn(*input_lfs)` = passthrough -> input returned unchanged; `is_passthrough_runtime = fn is _passthrough_fn` (line 1128) causes the output-contract boundary check to be SKIPPED (`and not is_passthrough_runtime`, line 1239-1244), so even ENFORCE_CONTRACTS does not catch the missing prediction column. (6) score_graph_lazy applies `.select(output_fields)` only when output_fields is truthy (line 825-827); when output_fields is None the missing column is never surfaced. validate_deploy (_validators.py:231-318) performs no per-modelScore configuration/bundling check; it would only catch the missing prediction column if the operator happened to supply test quotes whose `expected` mapping references that column (lines 198-208). tests/test_deploy_scorer_artifact_cache.py:255 covers the WITH-contract fail-loud path; the no-contract/no-model silent-passthrough case is unguarded and untested.

findings.title: Near-verbatim duplicate of haute._builders._declared_categorical_levels_for_model_score (different first arg only)
findings.description: This deploy helper and `_builders._declared_categorical_levels_for_model_score` (_builders.py:1132-1149) implement the same logic: seed one declaration for the modelScore node's own config, build candidate_ids via `list(dict.fromkeys([*source_ids, *(upstream_ids or [])]))`, append each candidate node's `config.get('categorical_levels')` when present, and call `merge_categorical_level_declarations`. The only differences are cosmetic: the deploy version takes a `node` (uses `node.id`/`node.data.config`) and seeds the owner label as `node.id`, while the builders version takes `config` and seeds the owner label as the literal `'modelScore'`; the owner label only affects the message in a conflict error. The two could share a single implementation (e.g. parameterised by an owner label), removing one of the duplicated bodies.
findings.evidence: Deploy (line 310-317): `declarations = [(node.id, node.data.config.get('categorical_levels'))]; candidate_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*source_ids, *(upstream_ids or [])])); declarations.extend((source_id, node_by_id[source_id].data.config.get('categorical_levels')) for source_id in candidate_ids if source_id in node_by_id); return merge_categorical_level_declarations(declarations)`. Builders (line 1141-1149): `declarations = [('modelScore', config.get('categorical_levels'))]; candidate_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([*source_ids, *(upstream_ids or [])])); ... (source_id, node_map[source_id].data.config.get('categorical_levels')) ... ; return merge_categorical_level_declarations(declarations)`. Identical control flow and merge call; only the seed owner label and the parameter shape differ.
findings.est_reduction: ~12 lines (consolidate two ~14-line helpers into one shared helper parameterised by owner label)
findings.behavior_preservation: Behaviour-preserving: merge output is identical for any inputs since the owner label only appears in the FeatureMismatchError raised on a conflicting declaration (source_node=owner); a shared helper can keep the deploy label as node.id and the builders label as 'modelScore' to preserve even those error messages verbatim.

findings.title: build_report reports post-truncation length as sampled_rows, breaking the sampled = scored + failed invariant
findings.description: When staging and production prediction lists differ in length, build_report truncates input_df to `scored` (line 427) and then reports `sampled_rows=len(input_df)` (line 449) using the already-truncated length. However `failed` (line 422) is computed against the ORIGINAL input_df length. The result is a self-contradictory report where sampled_rows != scored_rows + failed_rows: the header line in format_terminal/format_markdown shows '(N of total sampled)' with the wrong (too-small) N while simultaneously printing 'M rows failed to score', so a reviewer sees fewer sampled rows than the scored+failed rows actually accounted for. sampled_rows should be captured from the input length BEFORE truncation (the number of rows actually submitted for scoring).
findings.evidence: Line 421 `scored = min(len(staging_preds), len(prod_preds))`; line 422 `failed = len(input_df) - scored` (original length); lines 424-427 truncate `input_df = input_df.head(scored)`; line 449 `sampled_rows=len(input_df)` now reads the truncated length. Empirically confirmed with stg=[1 item], prd=[2 items], inp=2 rows -> ImpactReport(sampled_rows=1, scored_rows=1, failed_rows=1); invariant sampled==scored+failed is False (1 != 2). The existing test test_failed_rows_counted asserts only scored_rows/failed_rows and so does not catch the sampled_rows contradiction.

findings.title: build_report only aligns input_df to predictions when staging != prod length, causing an unhandled ShapeError (and negative failed_rows) when equal-length predictions are shorter than input_df
findings.description: The truncation guard at line 424 keys input_df alignment off `len(staging_preds) != len(prod_preds)` rather than off `scored < len(input_df)`. If staging and production predictions unwrap to the SAME length L but L < len(input_df) (e.g. both endpoints/envelopes return the same reduced row count, or an endpoint returns fewer predictions than inputs), input_df is left at its original length while stg_df/prd_df have L rows. _segment_breakdown (line 360) then builds pl.DataFrame({'seg': input_df[col], 'chg': change, ...}) with mismatched column heights and raises an unhandled polars ShapeError instead of a domain error or a consistent truncation. The same mismatch also makes `failed = len(input_df) - scored` correct only when truncation occurs; here failed stays positive but input_df is never trimmed, so segments crash. The fix is to always set input_df/preds to `scored` (and capture sampled_rows beforehand) regardless of staging-vs-prod equality.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: stg=12 identical dicts, prd=12 identical dicts (equal -> branch at line 424 skipped, input_df NOT truncated), inp=20 rows with a qualifying categorical column ('region' A*10+B*10). build_report raises `ShapeError: could not create a new DataFrame: height of column 'chg' (12) does not match height of column 'seg' (20)` from _segment_breakdown. No existing test exercises equal-length predictions shorter than input_df.

findings.est_reduction: ~3 lines / one redundant O(n) pass + redundant validation
findings.behavior_preservation: Result-identical: _percent_change_series is a pure function of (stg, prd, name); computing it once for the primary column and passing the series into _segment_breakdown yields the same change values and the same zero-baseline/non-finite raises (which already fire identically in _column_stats run first).
findings.title: Primary-column percent change is computed twice (in _column_stats and again in _segment_breakdown)
findings.description: build_report calls _column_stats(stg_df[primary], prd_df[primary], primary) which computes _percent_change_series (line 309), then calls _segment_breakdown for the same primary output_col which recomputes _percent_change_series on the identical columns (line 356), re-running _raise_for_non_finite_predictions and _zero_baseline_change_count a second time over the full series. The change series (or the precomputed ColumnStats source) could be threaded through to _segment_breakdown to avoid the duplicate pass and duplicate validation. Low impact but genuinely redundant on the hot path (full dataset width).

findings.title: _validate_base_image_pinning accepts newline-bearing base_image values (anchors use $ not \Z, and [^@] matches newlines)
findings.description:
The two pinning regexes use the `$` anchor and a `[^@]*` body that matches newline characters, so values containing newlines pass the 'is pinned' check. Concretely: (a) a trailing newline is accepted because `$` matches just before a final `
` (e.g. `'python:3.11.9-slim
'` -> accepted; `'python@sha256:'+'a'*64+'
'` -> accepted via _DIGEST_PINNED_RE.search); and (b) because the negated class `[^@]` (unlike `.`) DOES match `
`, a value such as `'python:3.11.9
RUN evil:latest'` is also accepted by _PATCH_PINNED_RE.match — the trailing `[^@]*` consumes the newline and following text, and `$` then matches end-of-string. This contradicts the function's own docstring, which states it 'Raises DeployError for every other form' and is the construction-time gate. The correct anchors are `\A`/`\Z`, and the body should exclude newlines (e.g. `[^@
]`).
findings.evidence:
Reproduced with the module's exact regexes: `_PATCH_PINNED_RE = ^[^:]+:[^@]*\d+\.\d+\.\d+[^@]*$` matches 'python:3.11.9-slim
' (span 0..19) and matches 'python:3.11.9
RUN evil:latest' (whole string). `_DIGEST_PINNED_RE = @sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` matches 'python@sha256:'+'a'*64+'
'. In Python, `$` (no re.MULTILINE) matches at end-of-string OR immediately before a trailing newline, and `[^@]` includes `
`. The docstring at lines 55-62 promises rejection of 'every other form'.

findings.title: Unreachable else-branch in _check allowed-keys computation (`_self` is always a set)
findings.description: In the dict-schema branch of `_check`, `top_keys = schema.get("_self", set())` always yields a `set` — every `_self` entry in the module-level `_VALID_TOML_SCHEMA` is a `set[str]`, and the default is `set()`. Therefore `allowed = top_keys | sub_sections if isinstance(top_keys, set) else sub_sections` can never take the `else sub_sections` path. The `isinstance(top_keys, set)` guard and its else arm are dead/unreachable defensive code for a shape the schema (and its type annotation `dict[str, set[str] | dict[str, set[str]]]`) never produces. The line can be simplified to `allowed = top_keys | sub_sections`.
findings.evidence: `_VALID_TOML_SCHEMA` (lines 151-181): every nested schema's `_self` value is a literal set (e.g. `"deploy": {"_self": {"target", ...}, ...}`, `"safety": {"_self": {"impact_dataset"}, ...}`, `"ci": {"_self": {"provider"}, ...}`). `schema.get("_self", set())` thus returns a set in all cases, so the ternary condition at line 201 is invariantly True and the `else` branch is unreachable.
findings.est_reduction: ~1 line (collapse ternary to a single expression)
findings.behavior_preservation: Identical: the `else` arm is never evaluated for any value of `_VALID_TOML_SCHEMA`; replacing the ternary with `top_keys | sub_sections` preserves all observable behavior.

findings.title: _validate_base_image / _validate_model_name accept a trailing newline (re.match + '$' anchor instead of fullmatch / \Z)
findings.description:
Both validators use `_RE.match(value)` against a pattern anchored with `^...$`. In Python, `$` matches at the end of the string OR immediately before a single trailing newline, so `re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9._:/@-]+$', 'python:3.11.9-slim
')` returns a match. Consequently `_validate_base_image('python:3.11.9-slim
')` and `_validate_model_name('motor
')` both PASS even though the value contains a control character the validators are meant to forbid. The docstrings state these exist to 'prevent command injection' / 'path traversal / injection', so silently admitting a trailing newline is a contract weakness. Practical blast radius is limited (a single trailing newline in `FROM {base_image}` only yields a blank Dockerfile line, and a multi-line `value
RUN ...` is still correctly rejected because text after the newline defeats the `$`), but the validators do not deliver the strict character whitelist they advertise. The existing test suite only covers an *interior* newline ('image
injection') and shell metacharacters, never a trailing newline, so the gap is unguarded.
findings.evidence:
Lines 25-26: `_VALID_BASE_IMAGE_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9._:/@-]+$")`, `_VALID_MODEL_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$")`. Lines 39 & 45 call `.match(...)`. Verified with the project venv: `base.match('python:3.11.9-slim
')` -> truthy, `name.match('motor
')` -> truthy, whereas `base.fullmatch('python:3.11.9-slim
')` -> None. Fix: use `re.fullmatch` (or anchor with `\A...\Z`). base_image then flows into Dockerfile `FROM {base_image}` (line 461) and model_name into the image tag `f"{model_name}:{git_sha}"` (line 142).

findings.title: build_and_push_image reuses a non-cleared .haute_build dir, baking stale artifacts from a prior run into the new image
findings.description: The build dir is created with `build_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)` and `artifacts_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)`, and is only removed in the `except BaseException` cleanup (lines 165-167). A SUCCESSFUL build therefore leaves `.haute_build/` (and `.haute_build/artifacts/`) on disk. A subsequent `build_and_push_image` call in the same working directory reuses that directory without clearing it: the manifest, Dockerfile and app.py are overwritten, but artifact files are only ever *added* (`shutil.copy2(artifact_path, artifacts_dir / artifact_name)`), never pruned. If the artifact set changes between runs (e.g. a model file is renamed, or a `.pkl` is replaced by a `.cbm`), the orphaned file from the previous run survives and is copied wholesale into the image by the Dockerfile's directory-level `COPY artifacts/ artifacts/` (line 471). The result is a container that silently ships a stale model artifact that is not referenced by the current manifest. Note the sibling MLflow path (`_mlflow.py`) is immune because it logs the live `artifact_path`s rather than copying into a reused directory, so this staleness is specific to the container target's copy+COPY model.
findings.evidence: Line 97-98 create/reuse build_dir; line 101-102 reuse artifacts_dir with exist_ok=True; lines 121-124 copy each current artifact in but nothing deletes pre-existing files; line 471 `COPY artifacts/ artifacts/` bundles everything in the dir; cleanup (rmtree) only runs in the `except BaseException` branch (166), so on success the dir persists for the next invocation. Tests `test_artifacts_copied_to_build_dir` and `test_cleanup_on_exception` only cover the single-run and exception paths, not a second run with a different artifact set.

findings.title: Artifact-remap loop unpacks an unused `artifact_path`; reducible to a dict comprehension over keys
findings.description: The remap loop iterates `resolved.artifacts.items()` and binds `artifact_path`, but the body only uses `artifact_name`. The whole block is a key-only transform and is more clearly written as a comprehension, avoiding the dead binding (which also masks the fact that the value is intentionally discarded).
findings.evidence: Lines 109-113: `container_artifacts: dict[str, str] = {}` then `for artifact_name, artifact_path in resolved.artifacts.items(): container_artifacts[artifact_name] = f"artifacts/{artifact_name}"`. `artifact_path` is never referenced. Equivalent: `manifest["artifacts"] = {name: f"artifacts/{name}" for name in resolved.artifacts}`.
findings.behavior_preservation: Identical output dict; pure refactor of a key-only mapping, no behavioral change.

findings.title: Serving signature silently maps every unrecognized Polars dtype (Decimal/Time/Duration/List/Struct/Binary/Object/Null) to string, producing a wrong serving contract
findings.description: `_to_colspecs` builds the MLflow ModelSignature from the resolved input/output schema dicts, whose values are `str(polars_dtype)` strings (see `infer_input_schema`/`infer_output_schema` in src/haute/deploy/_schema.py:71,141). It takes `base_type = dtype_str.split('(')[0]` and then `dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)`. `dtype_map` only covers integers, floats, String/Utf8, Boolean, Date, Datetime. Any other Polars dtype the pipeline legitimately produces -- `Decimal(...)` (e.g. a premium/money column), `Time`, `Duration`, `List(...)`, `Struct(...)`, `Categorical`, `Enum`, `Binary`, `Null`, `Object` -- has a base name not in the map and is SILENTLY coerced to `DataType.string`. The deployed Databricks Model Serving signature then advertises those columns as string, so the endpoint's input validation/coercion is wrong for those fields (a numeric Decimal column is described as text). This directly contradicts the project's 'fail loudly, no incorrect silent fallbacks' principle, and notably the sibling builder src/haute/modelling/_signature.py RAISES `ValueError('Unknown polars dtype ...')` on the very same dtype families (cataloged finding `signature-build-aborts-mlflow-run-on-temporal-decimal-features`) -- the deploy path takes the opposite, silent-and-wrong behavior. Evidence: `dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)` at line 244 with no membership check; e.g. `str(pl.Decimal(18,2))` -> 'Decimal(precision=18, scale=2)' -> base 'Decimal' -> not in dtype_map -> DataType.string.
findings.evidence: line 244: `mlflow_type = dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)` -- unknown base names default to string with no error. dtype_map (lines 221-237) lacks Decimal/Time/Duration/List/Struct/Categorical/Enum/Binary/Null/Object. Schema values are Polars `str(dtype)` strings (_schema.py:71 `{col: str(dtype) ...}`).

findings.title: Registered model version is re-derived via max(search_versions) instead of the value returned by log_model -- races to the wrong version and silently guesses "1" when the search is empty
findings.description: `mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(...)` returns a `ModelInfo` whose `registered_model_version` is the exact version just created (confirmed present in the installed mlflow 3.10.0: `ModelInfo.registered_model_version`). The code discards that return value and instead re-queries ALL versions of the UC model with `search_versions(client, uc_model_name)` and takes `max(versions, key=lambda v: int(v.version)).version`, falling back to the string `"1"` when `versions` is empty. Two defects: (1) Race/shared-state -- if another deploy of the same UC model registers a higher version between this `log_model` call and the `search_versions` call, `max()` returns that OTHER deploy's version, which is then passed as `model_version=int(latest_version)` to `_create_or_update_serving_endpoint` (line 152), so the live serving endpoint is bound to the wrong model version, and the wrong `v{model_version}` is reported to the user (cli/_deploy.py:201). (2) Silent incorrect fallback -- after a SUCCESSFUL `log_model` there is always at least one version; an empty `search_versions` result indicates a genuine registry problem, yet the `else: latest_version = "1"` branch fabricates version 1 and proceeds to serve/return it, masking the failure. This violates the project's 'no incorrect silent fallbacks / fail loudly' rule. Using `log_model(...).registered_model_version` eliminates both the race and the bogus fallback in one line.
findings.evidence: lines 124-131 call `mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(...)` but ignore its return; lines 135-140: `versions = search_versions(client, uc_model_name); if versions: latest_version = max(versions, key=lambda v: int(v.version)).version else: latest_version = "1"`; line 152 feeds `int(latest_version)` straight into the live endpoint. `ModelInfo.registered_model_version` exists in installed mlflow 3.10.0.

findings.title: Unreachable `if errors:` warning branch in validate_deploy (always-False after the raise)
findings.description: In `validate_deploy`, the block `if errors or test_quote_errors: ... raise DeployError(...)` (lines 319-330) raises whenever either error list is non-empty. Execution only continues past line 330 when BOTH `errors` and `test_quote_errors` are empty. The very next statement is `if errors: logger.warning("validation_failed", error_count=len(errors))` (lines 332-333) with an `else: logger.info("validation_passed")`. Because `errors` is provably empty at this point, the `if errors:` condition is always False and the `logger.warning(...)` on line 333 is unreachable dead code. Only the `else` branch (line 335, `validation_passed`) can ever run. This is a stale leftover from before `test_quote_errors` was folded into the line-319 guard: the function used to raise on `errors` alone, so this trailing `if errors:` once made sense; now it cannot. The entire 332-335 block reduces to a single `logger.info("validation_passed")`.
findings.evidence: Line 319 guard: `if errors or test_quote_errors:` -> raises on line 326. Reaching line 332 implies `not (errors or test_quote_errors)`, i.e. `errors == []`. Therefore `if errors:` at line 332 is always False; line 333 (`error_count=len(errors)`) never executes. Grep confirms the only `error_count=` + `validation_failed` reference in the codebase is this dead line itself, and no test asserts this warning fires (only `validation_passed` is reachable). Not covered by the three known findings (validate-time scoring w/o artifact_paths; SIMP-12 Decimal dedup; BUG-1 double-scoring).
findings.behavior_preservation: Removing the unreachable warning branch and keeping only `logger.info("validation_passed")` is exactly equivalent: the deleted code path is provably never taken, so no observable behavior (logs, return value, raises) changes for any input.

findings.title: validate_deploy parses every test-quote file twice (pre-check load_test_quote_file + score_test_quotes re-parse)
findings.description: Within a single `validate_deploy` call, each `*.json` in `test_quotes_dir` is JSON-parsed and case-validated twice. First, the missing-required-column pre-check loop (lines 296-309) calls `load_test_quote_file(jf)` -> `_load_test_quote_cases` -> `json.loads(read_user_text(path))` + `_parse_test_quote_case` per row. Immediately after, `score_test_quotes(resolved, tq_dir)` (line 312) re-globs the same directory and re-parses every file via `_load_test_quote_cases` (line 371). The file read, JSON decode, and full golden-row validation are therefore performed twice per file per `validate_deploy`. The pre-check needs the parsed rows only to diff column names against `input_schema`; `score_test_quotes` already parses the identical cases and could supply them (or the pre-check could be folded into the scoring loop). This is distinct from the known BUG-1, which concerns `handle_deploy` running the full scoring pass (score_graph) twice across `validate_deploy`+`handle_deploy`; here the duplicated work is the parse/validation inside `validate_deploy` itself.
findings.evidence: load_test_quote_file (line 116) -> `_load_test_quote_cases` (line 102) -> `json.loads(read_user_text(path))`. score_test_quotes (line 371) -> `_load_test_quote_cases(jf)` on the same files from the same `sorted(tq_dir.glob("*.json"))`. validate_deploy invokes both: pre-check loop at 296-309 and `score_test_quotes(resolved, tq_dir)` at 312. No caching of parsed cases between the two passes.
findings.est_reduction: ~10 LOC and one JSON parse + validation per test-quote file per validate_deploy (fold the column pre-check into the scoring loop, or have the scorer return/accept already-parsed cases)
findings.behavior_preservation: Parsing once and reusing the cases yields identical error detection: the same missing-column messages and the same scoring/expected-output errors are produced; only the redundant second parse is removed. Parse errors are still surfaced (currently as a parse error in the pre-check; consolidating must keep the same 'could not parse' message).

findings.title: _resolve_path has a dead `exists()` branch; both arms return the identical value
findings.description: After computing `pipeline_abs = (pipeline_dir / p).resolve()`, the function does `if pipeline_abs.exists(): return pipeline_abs` immediately followed by `return pipeline_abs`. Both branches return the exact same object, so the `pipeline_abs.exists()` check is dead — it has no observable effect and performs an unnecessary stat() syscall. The whole tail can be collapsed to a single `return pipeline_abs`. The surrounding docstring (lines 213-225) compounds the confusion: it describes a multi-step 'Resolution order' that prefers CWD when both exist ('The old code preferred CWD'), but the current code never consults CWD at all — relative paths are unconditionally resolved against `pipeline_dir`. The test `test_collect_artifacts_resolves_against_pipeline_dir_not_cwd` confirms the actual (single-path) behavior, and its sibling docstring at tests/test_deploy_config_and_bundle.py:13/247 still describes the obsolete 'tries CWD first' contract.
findings.est_reduction: ~4 lines of body collapsed to 1; plus an opportunity to fix the now-inaccurate docstring (no behavior change).
findings.behavior_preservation: Collapsing the two-arm tail to a single `return pipeline_abs` is exactly behavior-preserving: both arms already return the same `Path`. Removing the `.exists()` call only drops a redundant filesystem stat with no effect on the returned value (missing files are still caught downstream by `_check_exists`).

findings.title: _verify_static_source_schema treats a bare `schema` key as a schema declaration the read adapter never honors, causing a no-op file read
findings.description: `has_schema_declaration` (lines 173-175) gates the verification read on the presence of any of `schema_overrides`, `dtypes`, `column_dtypes`, or `schema`. For the first three, the read is meaningful: `read_data_source` -> `build_data_source_adapter` -> `_schema_overrides_from_config` (src/haute/_io.py:127-138) recognizes exactly `schema_overrides`/`dtypes`/`column_dtypes` and runs `_validate_declared_schema` during the read, so declared-dtype drift is enforced at the deploy boundary. But `_schema_overrides_from_config` does NOT recognize a bare `schema` key. So a static dataSource whose config carries only `schema` (and no `expected_columns`, no schema_overrides/dtypes/column_dtypes) passes the gate, performs a full `read_data_source(...).collect_schema()` whose `actual` is then discarded (the `if expected and ...` block at line 199 is skipped because `expected` is falsy), and validates nothing. The result is wasted deploy-time I/O plus a false impression that the `schema` declaration is being enforced, when it is silently ignored. This is an inconsistency between the gate's recognized keys and the adapter's recognized keys.
findings.evidence:
Gate at lines 173-176:
    has_schema_declaration = any(
        key in config for key in ("schema_overrides", "dtypes", "column_dtypes", "schema")
    )
    if not expected and not has_schema_declaration:
        return
Adapter recognition at src/haute/_io.py:127-138 (`_schema_overrides_from_config`) keys on only `schema_overrides`/`dtypes`/`column_dtypes` — `schema` is absent. findings.title: liveSwitch deploy pruning MAPPED (input_scenario_map) path silently selects the wrong live branch when two upstream labels collide under _sanitize_func_name (order-dependent, no ambiguity guard)
findings.description: When a liveSwitch node DOES have an input_scenario_map with a 'live' entry, _live_only_edges resolves the live edge by scanning the switch's incoming edges and taking the FIRST whose source label sanitizes to live_input_name (lines 59-64), then `break`s. The guard at lines 65-69 only raises when NO edge matches. It does NOT detect the case where TWO distinct upstream source nodes have labels that collide under _sanitize_func_name (e.g. 'Live Source' and 'Live-Source' both -> 'Live_Source', since sanitize maps both space and hyphen to '_'). In that case both edges 'match' live_input_name; whichever edge is listed first in graph.edges wins, the other live-candidate is dropped, and prune_for_deploy returns normally with NO error. The deployed scoring path therefore depends on edge ordering and can keep the WRONG upstream branch. This is the inverse of the already-known fallback finding: the known finding (bucket 'known', verdict refuted) asserts the mapped path is the safe one that 'raises on no-match/collision, unlike the fallback' — this finding shows the mapped path is ALSO silently order-dependent on COLLISION (it only raises on no-match, not on ambiguous-match). It is also distinct from the codegen B3 finding, which concerns two input_scenario_map keys both mapped to 'live' (duplicate map VALUES); here the map has a single 'live' key but two SOURCE LABELS collide after sanitization.
findings.evidence: Executed repro (temp script, project root sandboxed, then deleted). Graph: nodes a='Live Source'(dataSource), b='Live-Source'(dataSource) [both sanitize to 'Live_Source'], switch=liveSwitch config={input_scenario_map:{'Live_Source':'live','Other':'batch'}, inputs:['Live_Source','Other']}, output. Edges to switch ordered (a,b) vs (b,a). prune_for_deploy(graph,'output') returned with NO exception in both cases; surviving switch parent = {'a'} for order (a,b) and {'b'} for order (b,a). So the kept live branch flips with edge order and exactly one colliding source is silently chosen. Code trace: line 60 `if e.target == sid`; line 62 `if _sanitize_func_name(src_label) == live_input_name`; line 63 sets switch_live_source[sid]=e.source; line 64 `break` -> first-match-wins; the line 65 `if sid not in switch_live_source` guard never fires because a (colliding) match was found.

findings.title: Duplicated 'first incoming edge whose sanitized source label matches live_input_name' scan in both branches of _live_only_edges
findings.description: The fallback branch (lines 52-57) and the mapped branch (lines 59-64) contain a verbatim-identical edge-scan loop: `for e in edges: if e.target == sid: src_label = node_map[e.source].data.label; if _sanitize_func_name(src_label) == live_input_name: switch_live_source[sid] = e.source; break`. The only difference is the surrounding guard (fallback gates on `if live_input_name:` and never raises; mapped raises at 65-69 when unmatched). Extracting the shared loop into a single helper, e.g. `_first_source_matching_label(edges, sid, node_map, live_input_name) -> str | None`, and having each branch call it (mapped raising on None, fallback leaving switch_live_source unset on None) removes the duplication and makes the live-resolution rule single-sourced, which also makes the collision behavior in the related bug finding visible in one place.
findings.evidence: Lines 52-57 and 59-64 are character-for-character the same loop body apart from indentation; both iterate `edges`, filter `e.target == sid`, sanitize `node_map[e.source].data.label`, compare to `live_input_name`, assign `switch_live_source[sid]`, and `break`.
findings.behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving: a shared helper iterates `edges` in the same order and returns the same first match (or None); mapped path raises on None exactly as today (lines 65-69), fallback path leaves switch_live_source[sid] unset on None exactly as today. No change to which edges survive.

All 9 in-scope functions reviewed in full across src/haute/deploy/__init__.py, _model_code.py, _utils.py, with dependencies traced into _config.py (ResolvedDeploy/resolve_config/_CONTAINER_BASED_TARGETS), _scorer.py (score_graph/admit_deploy_execution), _mlflow.py + _container.py (the two manifest consumers), _validators.py, _bundler.py, and _execution_admission.py (admission lifecycle). No NEW bugs or simplifications of genuine value found; not re-reporting the known _model_code.py finding about the validate-time test-quote gate. Items considered and deliberately NOT reported: (1) _validate_target/_dispatch_resolved set arithmetic (_CONTAINER_PLATFORM_TARGETS = _CONTAINER_BASED_TARGETS - {container}; _PLANNED_TARGETS={sagemaker,azure-ml}) is correct and exhaustive; the trailing 'Unhandled deploy target' raise is genuinely unreachable but already marked # pragma: no cover as a reasonable defensive guard. (2) predict() acquires an admission context via admit_deploy_execution BEFORE pl.from_pandas(); a raise from from_pandas could leak an in-flight reservation (DEPLOY_BATCH profile, row_count>1) since only score_graph->plan.cleanup releases it — but create_admitted_execution_context registers weakref.finalize(context, admission_release) (line 464), which releases on GC, so it is a delayed release, not a true leak; DEPLOY_LIVE never reserves at all. Not reportable. (3) predict()'s params arg is unused but is part of MLflow's pyfunc predict contract. (4) load_context builds self._artifact_paths = manifest['artifacts'] intersected with context.artifacts; in deploy_to_mlflow all resolved.artifacts (incl. bundled feature contracts) are registered, so the intersection never silently drops a real artifact. (5) build_manifest's 'nodes_skipped_names' actually stores resolved.removed_node_ids (node IDs, not human names) — a naming/stringly smell, but it is informational-only metadata never read at runtime by either consumer (confirmed via grep of manifest key reads) and is explicitly asserted by tests; likewise build_manifest['pipeline_file'] may be a relative path but is also pure metadata never consumed at runtime. (6) get_user/get_haute_version catch only the narrow expected exceptions (KeyError/OSError, PackageNotFoundError) and otherwise fail loudly, matching the project's no-fallback philosophy.
